A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research by the same authors, despite the shortened title and substantial theoretical revision. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 Section 8 reports original CartPole experiments, including baseline comparisons, deployment perturbations, and dual-network capacity sweeps in Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v2 Section 7 retains these original CartPole experiments and their results in Figures 1–3.

M1.justification: RFL-TV becomes RFL-ϕ: the scalar TV hinge-loss dual is generalized to two dual functions, gη and gν, with a convex-conjugate loss for ϕ-divergence robust backups and confidence sets. This changes the proposed procedure beyond renaming. The practical CartPole algorithm remains the TV implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CartPole-v1 under the same action-randomization, force-magnitude, and pole-length perturbations. The added χ² and KL treatment is theoretical; neither version reports experiments using those divergences or additional environments.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains DQN, GOLF, and GOLF-DUAL; Figure 2 retains OPROVI-TV at the same robustness radii. Citation renumbering does not change comparator membership. The expanded theoretical comparisons in Table 1 are not additional experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The perturbation grids, nominal training environment, return metric, configuration selection, and experimental settings remain unchanged. Both retain 500 training episodes, horizon 500, discount 0.99, batch size 256, and the same robustness and slack sweeps.

E4.justification: The same robustness comparisons and Figure 3 sensitivity analysis are retained. Both vary dual-network widths across (64,64), (128,128), and (256,256), with robustness radii 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6. The revised appendices add theory rather than empirical supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 evaluation episodes, three independent seeds {0,1,2}, and 95% confidence intervals computed across seeds and episodes. No repeated-run counts or empirical uncertainty-reporting procedures change.

E6.justification: All nine plotted panels in Figures 1–3 retain identical plotting content, including curves and uncertainty bands. The accompanying return comparisons and qualitative experimental findings are unchanged. Table 1's revised asymptotic guarantees are theoretical changes assessed under T1.

T1.justification: The robust-coverability and cumulative-visitation analysis is replaced by robust DE/BE definitions, new rank/Eluder relationships, and counting lemmas. v2 adds general ϕ-duality, bounded-dual assumptions, and TV/χ²/KL guarantees, and revises the linear specialization. The failure-state assumption is retained for TV and moved to Appendix 9.2, not deleted.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion shift from TV-specific learning governed by supposedly necessary robust coverability to broader ϕ-divergence learning governed by robust BE dimension without coverage or concentrability assumptions. This substantially redefines the central contribution and claimed applicability.

C2.justification: v1 explains learnability through nominal-versus-worst-case coverage deficits and discusses favorable and unfavorable coverage regimes. v2 replaces that interpretation with intrinsic BE complexity, adds divergence-specific smoothing and 'robustness helps' explanations, and qualifies linear guarantees as reductions under small robust BE dimension. Empirical interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Tables 2–3 and practical Algorithm 2 retain the same network architectures, optimizer settings, replay buffer, target updates, exploration schedule, and training details. Reformatting the pseudocode does not change its implementation information. No new code/data access or hardware disclosure is supplied.

R1.justification: The work is repositioned from coverage-based online robust learning to a robust extension of the Bellman–Eluder framework. Jin et al.'s already-cited BE work becomes central to the analysis and comparisons. v2 also adds Duchi–Namkoong and Shapiro citations while removing several earlier coverage, offline-learning, and linear-RL references.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and theoretical narrative are extensively rewritten. v2 adds a dedicated comparison subsection, moves the linear specialization into Appendix 9.3, reorganizes the appendices, and places references after them. These are substantial editorial and structural changes.

P2.justification: Table 1 is expanded and reformatted with a divergence column and grouped TV/χ²/KL rows. Algorithm 2 is compressed and relocated, and existing figures and tables are resized or repositioned. The experimental plots and Tables 2–3 retain their substantive display content.

improvement.justification: The broader dual formulation and explicit BE connections offer potential gains, but the central replacement guarantee has unresolved justification. Unlike v1's explicit occupancy-ratio transfer, v2 Lemma K.1 moves from a worst-case-occupancy identity in Equation 74 to nominal-occupancy residuals in Equations 67–68 without establishing that transition. This affects the advertised coverage-free guarantee. With experimental evidence unchanged, the net quality effect of the theoretical expansion cannot be reliably determined.
